scope: Proposition 7.4 (Cone correction) of the manuscript “The trace cone classifies Razak–Jacelon stabilizations” (preprints/The-trace-cone-classifies-Razak-Jacelon-stabilizations-September-25-2026/The-trace-cone-classifies-Razak-Jacelon-stabilizations-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 301 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9cf38a67706f91fa), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 51-52. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose h : S → D is c.p.c. and satisfies (7.1). After trace-preserving coordinate corner padding, there is a homomorphism λ : S → D such that (λ − hpad )(S(U)) ⊂ J(U) (U ⊂ X open). (7.23) 51 The padding can be chosen to fix the constant copy of Q in the sequence quotient. Consequently it preserves the constant ideal comparisons and the regularized trace formulas prescribed for h.
